correctness.rationale: Connected graph Laplacian forces all vertices to fire an equal count in any three-round periodic orbit. For primitive period three that count is one or two. Fix one hub phase and enumerate each triangle's feasible peripheral firing phases; precisely three ordered choices have feasible chip intervals. With a synchronous-pair triangles, 0<=r<=k−a−1 hub excess choices give one-firing mass 3k+a+r and coefficient 3 sum_{a<=j}binom(k,a)2^(k−a) for 0<=j<k. Chip complement Cσ(v)=2deg(v)−1−σ(v) commutes with the update on bounded periodic states and reflects masses across 10k−1, establishing high band and completeness. Sum of coefficients yields 12k3^(k−1); size-biased B=1+Bin(k−1,2/3) and uniform hub excess yield two uniform limit intervals. Independent direct bounded-state simulation yielded k=2 total72 and k=3 total324 with exact mass histograms, matching the analytic polynomial. Finite simulation is corroboration, not the all-k proof.
